nodes.label: Phase 3 Business API Reference
nodes.rationale: Base path /api, JSON responses; only endpoints that exist are documented - unimplemented LLM summaries and SHAP explanations have no routes.

nodes.label: Bearer JWT Authentication
nodes.rationale: Identity from the JWT sub claim, authority from public.profiles.role read server-side. ES256 via JWKS for this project with HS256 legacy support; algorithm pinned and iss, aud, exp and a UUID sub all asserted. A 503 rather than 401 means the backend could not determine how to verify tokens.

nodes.label: VIEWER Profile Provisioning On Signup
nodes.rationale: A profiles row is created by the on_auth_user_created trigger with role VIEWER as a hard-coded literal, never from signup metadata. An authenticated user with no profile row gets 403, not a default role.

nodes.label: 400 vs 422 Distinction
nodes.rationale: 400 means 'this is not shaped like a request'; 422 means 'this is a valid request the domain refuses' - land acquired exceeding land required, or project data too incomplete for a snapshot. 409 covers duplicate codes and existing 1:1 records; 503 a dependency outage. Raw database text is never returned.

nodes.label: API Role Permission Matrix
nodes.rationale: ADMIN full; ANALYST and VIEWER read nationally; OFFICER reads and writes assigned projects only. 'Assigned' means an explicit project_assignments row or having created the project, mirroring is_assigned_to_project() in the schema.

nodes.label: Projects Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Paginated, filtered, role-scoped list plus create (ADMIN), read, patch and delete. DELETE cascades to child data but is refused with 409 if a prediction references one of its snapshots - the audit trail of what was predicted must not be erasable.

nodes.label: created_by Rejected From Input
nodes.rationale: created_by is set from the authenticated caller and rejected if supplied, because authorship grants project access - accepting it from input would let a caller hand access to someone else.

nodes.label: Land Acquisition Endpoint
nodes.rationale: 1:1 with project. Supplying land_acquisition_percentage returns 400 because the column is GENERATED ALWAYS STORED. Rules: acquired <= required, parcels acquired <= total, notification <= award <= possession, no negatives.

nodes.label: Compensation Endpoint
nodes.rationale: 1:1 with project; compensation_pending and compensation_pending_percentage are database-calculated and supplying either returns 400. payment_status vocabulary NOT_STARTED / IN_PROGRESS / PARTIAL / COMPLETED / DISPUTED.

nodes.label: Amounts And Areas Are Strings
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL NUMERIC is exact decimal and an IEEE-754 double cannot hold every value, so callers send strings, receive strings and must not parse them to Number for arithmetic.

nodes.label: Legal Issues Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Many per project, addressed as (projectId, id); requesting one through a different project returns 404 - knowing its UUID is not enough to reach it. case_reference only when court_case is true.

nodes.label: Risk Factors Endpoints
nodes.rationale: factor_type is a foreign key into risk_factor_types rather than a fixed enum, so new factor types are an INSERT not a schema change; an unknown code returns 422 pointing at GET /api/reference/risk-factor-types, which frontends should use to populate dropdowns rather than hard-coding a list that will go stale.

nodes.label: GET /api/projects/:projectId/full
nodes.rationale: Everything about one project in a single round trip; six reads run concurrently, one query per table regardless of child row count. Snapshots are summarised rather than returned in full, and summary counts live (OPEN / IN_PROGRESS) issues only because a resolved dispute is history, not current risk.

nodes.label: Feature Snapshot Endpoints
nodes.rationale: POST creates a snapshot with no request body - features are derived from current project data and the timestamp is the server clock, because backdating would corrupt the temporal integrity of the training set. A preview endpoint dry-runs the same computation and writes nothing.

nodes.label: data_quality Computed Not Stored
nodes.rationale: project_feature_snapshots has no provenance column and Phase 3 does not add one, so the data_quality block (issues, missingFeatures, sources, completeness) is returned for the caller to persist if needed.

nodes.label: The 21 Snapshot Features
nodes.rationale: Land, compensation, social scale, legal flags, risk-factor flags and elapsed time. Derived numerics are copied from the generated columns rather than recomputed in JavaScript to avoid float drift and disagreement with the source row; litigation_flag derives from court_cases_count so the two cannot disagree; notification_delay_days is null when the notification predates the planned start because a clamp to 0 would assert something the data does not say.

nodes.label: Snapshot Refusal (422)
nodes.rationale: Creation is refused when the data cannot support an honest feature vector: no land record, missing required/acquired hectares, acquired > required, percentage outside 0-100, or a future date. Warnings (missing compensation, notification or planned start) are returned alongside a successful snapshot instead.

nodes.label: Snapshot Immutability At Every Layer
nodes.rationale: No PATCH and no DELETE route exists, the service exposes no such method, and the database grants no UPDATE policy, has no updated_at column and restricts deletion of a referenced snapshot. Snapshots are never created as a side effect of editing project data, because auto-snapshotting would make 'which snapshot did this prediction use' meaningless.

nodes.label: Prediction And Assessment Endpoints
nodes.rationale: POST runs resolve-snapshot, call ML, evaluate rules, generate recommendations, persist and return. Snapshot resolution order: supplied id validated against the project, else latest, else a new one. 503 if the ML service is unreachable with nothing persisted; 422 if it returns no delay estimate. No PATCH or DELETE, because editing a prediction would destroy the only basis on which a past decision can be reviewed.

nodes.label: The Two Signals Are Never Merged
nodes.rationale: risk_assessment comes from the deterministic rule engine; predicted_delay_days is the historical median carrying no project-specific signal. There is no combined 'AI confidence' score and there will not be one - averaging a deterministic score with a figure that has no predictive content produces a number that looks authoritative and means nothing.

nodes.label: assessment_complete Flag
nodes.rationale: assessment_complete: false means core inputs were missing, so a low risk_score reflects incomplete records as much as low risk; missing_inputs names what is absent and the result must not be presented as reassurance.

nodes.label: Assessments Are Read Back, Never Recomputed
nodes.rationale: GET /assessment returns the stored prediction row, ranked explanations and recommendations; re-running the rules against today's data would answer a different question from the one the endpoint is asked. Explanations carry explanation_source RULE_ENGINE to keep rule contributions distinct from model self-attribution.

nodes.label: Deliberately Absent Routes
nodes.rationale: No SHAP explanations (explaining a model that loses to a median baseline would dress up noise as insight), no LLM summaries or dashboard analytics (Phase 6), and no API surface for actual_outcomes - which is part of why outcome data cannot reach a prediction.
